title: Two response methods, two different contracts
summary: Ordinary-flight Step Response and CHIRP Frequency Response both study setpoint-to-gyro behaviour, but they do not produce interchangeable evidence.

blocks.text: Airframe divides setpoint and filtered gyro into overlapping two-second windows, rejects windows without enough excitation, applies a Hamming taper, performs regularized Wiener deconvolution, smooths and integrates the impulse estimate, then averages accepted responses over the first 500 ms. The displayed peak, half-response latency, and 10–90% rise time describe that estimate—not a literal collection of stick steps.

With complete modern CHIRP debug data, Airframe estimates magnitude, phase, sensitivity, coherence, bandwidth, resonance, and a derived step response by axis. The tune score is withheld when required metrics, axes, runs, reliable coverage, or frequency span are insufficient. Its confidence is evidence quality, not an extra handful of score points.

blocks.title: Legacy CHIRP is not modern CHIRP
blocks.text: Betaflight 2025.12.2 can log the CHIRP mode and phase while leaving the later axis, frequency, and excitation debug channels at zero. Airframe may still estimate ordinary-flight Step Response from setpoint and gyro, but it correctly withholds Frequency Response.
